metadata.focus_area: VMA usage, buffer creation, staging patterns, memory types

findings.title: Deprecated VMA_MEMORY_USAGE enums used instead of VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO
findings.description: The createBuffer() helper uses the legacy VMA memory usage enums (VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_CPU_TO_GPU, VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_CPU_ONLY, VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_GPU_ONLY) which are deprecated since VMA v3. The new VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO combined with host access flags allows VMA to make smarter memory type decisions, especially on hardware with unified memory or ReBAR support.
findings.recommendation: Replace legacy usage enums with VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO plus appropriate VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_SEQUENTIAL_WRITE_BIT or VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_RANDOM_BIT flags. Refactor createBuffer() to accept VmaAllocationCreateFlags as well.

findings.title: Staging buffer missing VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_SEQUENTIAL_WRITE_BIT flag
findings.description: The staging buffer in uploadBuffer() is created with VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_CPU_ONLY but does not set VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_SEQUENTIAL_WRITE_BIT. While the deprecated CPU_ONLY still works, the modern flag enables VMA to pick the optimal memory type for sequential write access patterns (the pattern used here with memcpy).
findings.recommendation: Use VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO with VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_SEQUENTIAL_WRITE_BIT for staging buffers.
findings.vulkan_spec_reference: VMA documentation: Recommended usage patterns - Staging copy

findings.title: Uniform buffers use VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_CPU_TO_GPU without HOST_ACCESS flags
findings.description: Uniform buffers are created with VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_CPU_TO_GPU and then persistently mapped. The modern recommended approach is VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO with VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_SEQUENTIAL_WRITE_BIT and VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_MAPPED_BIT, which may also allow VMA to use device-local + host-visible memory (BAR) when available.
findings.recommendation: Use VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO with VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_HOST_ACCESS_SEQUENTIAL_WRITE_BIT | VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_MAPPED_BIT. With MAPPED_BIT, VMA returns the persistently mapped pointer in VmaAllocationInfo::pMappedData, eliminating the need for a separate vmaMapMemory call.
findings.vulkan_spec_reference: VMA documentation: Recommended usage patterns - Advanced data uploading

findings.title: Uniform buffers not unmapped during cleanup
findings.description: The uniform buffers are persistently mapped via vmaMapMemory() in createUniformBuffers() (line 428) but vmaUnmapMemory() is never called before destruction. While VMA handles this gracefully during vmaDestroyBuffer(), it is not clean practice. The mapping count may not match.
findings.recommendation: Either call vmaUnmapMemory() before vmaDestroyBuffer() for each uniform buffer, or use VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_MAPPED_BIT so VMA manages the persistent mapping lifecycle automatically.

findings.title: Missing pipeline barrier after staging buffer transfer to device-local memory
findings.description: In uploadBuffer(), after vkCmdCopyBuffer() completes the transfer from staging to device-local buffer, there is no pipeline memory barrier inserted to ensure the transfer write is visible before subsequent vertex/index buffer reads. The code relies on vkQueueWaitIdle() for host synchronization, but there is no device-side barrier for the buffer's memory to transition from TRANSFER_WRITE to VERTEX_ATTRIBUTE_READ / INDEX_READ. In practice this works because all geometry uploads happen during initialization before any rendering, and vkQueueWaitIdle provides an implicit full pipeline barrier. However, if uploadBuffer() were ever called during rendering, this would be a synchronization bug.
findings.recommendation: Insert a VkBufferMemoryBarrier after vkCmdCopyBuffer with srcStageMask=VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFER_BIT, dstStageMask=VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_VERTEX_INPUT_BIT, srcAccessMask=VK_ACCESS_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT, dstAccessMask=VK_ACCESS_VERTEX_ATTRIBUTE_READ_BIT|VK_ACCESS_INDEX_READ_BIT. This makes the transfer safe even if called at runtime.

findings.title: No error checking on vmaCreateBuffer and vmaCreateImage return values
findings.description: The createBuffer() helper does not check the VkResult returned by vmaCreateBuffer(). Similarly, createDepthResources() (line 252) does not check the result of vmaCreateImage(). If allocation fails (e.g., out of GPU memory), the code will proceed with null/invalid handles, leading to undefined behavior or crashes.
findings.recommendation: Check the VkResult returned by vmaCreateBuffer() and vmaCreateImage() and throw a std::runtime_error on failure, consistent with other Vulkan call sites in the codebase.

findings.title: No error checking on vmaMapMemory return value
findings.description: The vmaMapMemory() calls in createUniformBuffers() (line 428) and uploadBuffer() (line 715) do not check the returned VkResult. If mapping fails, the code would use a null/garbage pointer for memcpy, causing undefined behavior.
findings.recommendation: Check return value of vmaMapMemory() and throw on failure.

findings.title: vkQueueWaitIdle used for staging transfer synchronization instead of fence
findings.description: uploadBuffer() uses vkQueueWaitIdle() to wait for the transfer to complete. This stalls the entire graphics queue, blocking any other pending work. For initialization-only uploads this is acceptable, but it serializes all 4 buffer uploads (2 vertex + 2 index) unnecessarily. A single batch submission with a fence, or using a dedicated transfer queue, would be more efficient.
findings.recommendation: Batch all geometry uploads into a single command buffer or use a VkFence for per-transfer synchronization. For init-time uploads, a single command buffer with all copies followed by one vkQueueWaitIdle would be more efficient than 4 separate submit-and-wait cycles.

findings.title: Depth image created with deprecated VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_GPU_ONLY without dedicated allocation flag
findings.description: The depth image uses VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_GPU_ONLY (deprecated) and does not set VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_DEDICATED_MEMORY_BIT. The VMA documentation recommends dedicated allocations for large, frequently recreated resources like render targets and depth buffers. The depth image is recreated on every swapchain resize.
findings.recommendation: Use VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO with VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_DEDICATED_MEMORY_BIT for the depth image, as recommended by VMA docs for render targets that are frequently recreated.
findings.vulkan_spec_reference: VMA documentation: Recommended usage patterns - GPU-only resources

findings.title: Single command pool used for both rendering and transfer operations
findings.description: uploadBuffer() allocates one-time transfer command buffers from m_commandPool, the same pool used for rendering command buffers. The rendering pool uses VK_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER_BIT. Using a separate transient command pool with VK_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_TRANSIENT_BIT for short-lived transfer commands would allow the driver to optimize memory allocation for those command buffers.
findings.recommendation: Create a separate command pool with VK_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_TRANSIENT_BIT for one-time transfer command buffers.

findings.title: AllocatedBuffer and AllocatedImage structs have uninitialized members
findings.description: The AllocatedBuffer and AllocatedImage structs do not initialize their members to null/zero by default. While VulkanApp initializes them with {} (value-initialization), if these structs are used elsewhere without value-initialization, the handles would contain garbage values, making error detection and conditional cleanup unreliable.
findings.recommendation: Initialize members to VK_NULL_HANDLE/nullptr: VkBuffer buffer = VK_NULL_HANDLE; VmaAllocation allocation = VK_NULL_HANDLE; etc.

findings.title: No error checking on vkQueueSubmit in uploadBuffer
findings.description: The vkQueueSubmit() call in uploadBuffer() does not check the return VkResult, unlike the same call in drawFrame() (line 536) which does check. If submission fails, the code proceeds to wait on the queue and destroy the staging buffer without the transfer having occurred.
findings.evidence:
vkQueueSubmit(m_graphicsQueue, 1, &submitInfo, VK_NULL_HANDLE);  // No error check
vkQueueWaitIdle(m_graphicsQueue);
findings.recommendation: Check the return value of vkQueueSubmit() and throw on failure, consistent with the drawFrame() error handling pattern.

top_concerns: All VMA memory usage enums are deprecated (VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_CPU_TO_GPU, CPU_ONLY, GPU_ONLY) -- should migrate to VMA_MEMORY_USAGE_AUTO with appropriate host access flags
Missing pipeline barrier after buffer transfer could cause synchronization issues if uploadBuffer is used at runtime
No error checking on vmaCreateBuffer, vmaCreateImage, vmaMapMemory, and vkQueueSubmit in transfer path -- silent failures lead to undefined behavior
Four separate submit-and-wait cycles for geometry upload is suboptimal; batching would improve init time
